- The installer's skill-name deletion list now requires each name to be a plain basename matching the same strict pattern — anything else is dropped, never deleted.

Doc-accuracy pass: honest security-scan provenance, clearer config help, a named dead-code heuristic, and a churn-resilient per-platform escalation footer.

### Changed
- SECURITY.md's SkillSpector section now pins the version it was actually last scanned against and states scanning is periodic, not per-release — replacing wording that implied a version bump alone kept the scan current.
- `autoScanFileCapSlice`'s help text clarified: it is a file count, not a fraction.
- rot-canary's "dead code" heuristic is now named explicitly: zero-reference reachability across all entry routes (reflection, DI, events, public API, tests), not a single-file grep.
- The shared escalation footer's stale "no concurrent fan-out" platform list dropped — all three named platforms have since shipped parallel subagent support — replaced with a note to verify the platform's current capability, since this class of fact churns.

body:
Ships the config-loss fix to users — earlier post-3.7.3 commits had kept the version number unchanged, so `claude plugin update` never delivered them.

### Fixed
- `.coalmine.json` no longer silently reverts to defaults. The JSONC comment-stripper desynced on a string value ending in a backslash immediately before a later `//` — it leaked escape state, mis-stripped that later comment, `JSON.parse` threw, and the failure was swallowed, silently falling back to all defaults (a config-write path had the same bug and could wipe a user's config). Replaced with one shared, string-aware stripper used by the hook, `configure.mjs`, and `verify.mjs` alike.
- Thai-language text no longer leaks into two skills' `SKILL.md` bodies — removed; skills stay English, and runtime output still mirrors the user's own language.
- The installer now sweeps a retired skill name even with no install manifest present — a pre-manifest install from before the `rotcanary` → `rot-canary` rename could leave the old skill directory behind on upgrade, so an agent reading `.agents/skills` (e.g. Antigravity) kept listing a duplicate command.

### Changed
- Added `CONTRIBUTING.md`; trimmed README/SECURITY for length and heading order; moved the `eval/` benchmark to the series umbrella; restored the "measurement" design principle. SECURITY.md's SkillSpector section now records an actual completed scan run with full provenance, replacing an earlier "binary not executed" note.

A CodeQL/security hardening pass, the series doctrine's move to the org, and a CI cleanup.

### Changed
- The series doctrine (Phoenix-13 hooks-safety + scripts-quality) moved to the org's canonical home; this repo dropped its own `docs/` copies, `SECURITY.md` links the org copy instead, and the doctrine-mirror gate now checks only the two machine-local rule homes.

### Fixed
- Closed a CodeQL `js/file-system-race` finding: the installer and `configure.mjs` now read-and-handle-ENOENT instead of check-then-read/write, and the size-tripwire check reads via one open file descriptor instead of a separate stat then read. All were benign in context; the remaining by-design findings are dismissed with documented reasons.
- Disabled markdownlint's new MD060 table-column-style rule — this repo's compact tables are valid GFM.
- The README now states the detection-benchmark's run date inline instead of only behind a link.

### Security
- Workflow actions pinned to commit SHAs (with a version comment), replacing floating major-version tags — closes the OpenSSF Scorecard PinnedDependencies findings; Dependabot still tracks them for updates.

body:
A path-traversal guard bypass on Windows in the manifest-integrity check, caught by rot-canary's own auto-scan on the v3.5.0 code the same day it shipped.

### Fixed
- The manifest integrity guard split its keys on `/` only, so a hand-crafted manifest key using Windows backslashes could slip past it — `verify.mjs <target>` would then resolve and hash a file outside the install target (a read-only info-disclosure oracle). Replaced with a resolve-and-contain check that handles forward slashes, backslashes, absolute paths, and drive-relative paths uniformly. Same path-traversal class as an earlier `safeSkillNames` fix, resurfacing the moment new security-relevant code shipped.

body:
Self-consistency + installed-artifact integrity checks land, plus a second, independent eval engine confirms rot-canary's detection quality.

### Added
- A self-consistency layer (`scripts/consistency.mjs`) mechanically cross-checks the artifacts an agent trusts but never verifies: canary-count agreement between `skills/` and `plugin.json`, byte-identical doctrine mirrors across every rule home, and well-formed freshness stamps.
- Installed-artifact integrity: the installer now records a SHA-256 of every file it writes, and `node scripts/verify.mjs <target>` re-hashes the installed tree and flags any file changed or missing since install — a surface git never sees. Path-traversal-guarded.
- gold-standard's RE-VALIDATE pass now flags a memory/decision-log or rule-register entry that contradicts a binding rule or another decision, or names a file/flag/command that no longer exists.
- A second, independent eval engine (Antigravity) ran the rot-canary detection corpus blind: 13/13 recall, 0 false positives on the clean decoys, 12/13 correct severity — the one disagreement sits exactly in the predicted severity-judgment band. README and the eval results now show both engines.
- The Eval harness itself (`eval/`): an AV-Comparatives-style detection-rate measurement — 16 rot-canary fixtures (12 with planted, line-labeled defects across all 7 categories, 4 clean decoys), a mechanical scorer, and model-stamped results. Baseline run: 13/13 recall, 0 false positives on the decoys.
- The Phoenix Commandments (hooks-safety) and scripts-quality doctrine are now published in-repo under `docs/` — the design-principles doc had linked them at a gitignored path nobody on GitHub could open. A repo-wide link audit found no other broken links.
- hooks-safety doctrine gains a Hermetic Hook Testing section (spawn the real hook in a sandboxed environment, assert exit code/silence/state) — proposed by an independent model's doctrine review whose verdicts matched the existing stamps.

### Fixed
- `configure.mjs` now errors on a trailing boolean flag given with no value, instead of silently writing `false`. The eval scorer's confusing no-op exit line was dropped.

The fat-trim release — same rules and behavior, fewer tokens spent injecting them every session.

### Changed
- Conductor injection cut 37% (1930 → 1218 chars) — the per-key config list replaced by a pointer to the commented config file.
- The Stop-hook nudge tail trimmed ~40% in all 5 languages — it had been duplicating what the invoked skill already instructs; now just the confirmed-only-report rule, the fix-menu offer, and the kill-switch path.
- The duplicated config-loading plumbing across the standalone hooks (Node and PowerShell) now lives once in a shared source, synced into every hook file at build time — `verify.mjs` fails on drift, and each hook stays a single portable file.
- The 22-key config schema moved to one table-driven source shared by `verify.mjs` (a validation loop instead of per-key hand-written checks) and `configure.mjs` (flags, parsing, validation, and `--help` all generated from the table) — a gate test now asserts help documents every key.
- The escalation heading and its table header, previously duplicated across all 9 skill sources, are now deduplicated into one shared partial (rendered output unchanged).

body:
The config release — a documented, validated `.coalmine.json` schema, plus a batch of fixes from an issue review.

### Added
- A categorized `.coalmine.json` config system: a 22-key schema in 4 commented groups (interactive behavior, scan and watch limits, re-validation cadences, enterprise paths). The installer drops a fully documented copy at the project root — zero-config defaults for everyone, overrides for anyone who wants them. `configure.mjs` edits it with validation and legacy-key migration; `verify.mjs` type-checks every key; hooks read it dynamically.
- Hooks now resolve `.coalmine.json` from the git root rather than the current directory, so config is honored when the agent works from a subdirectory. The installer supports worktree/submodule `.git` files and refuses to target CoalMine's own source `skills/` directory.
- An auto-scan token cap: past a configured file count, only the most recently touched files are scanned, with a localized notice appended (all 5 languages).

### Fixed
- Touched files are now recorded as absolute paths in both the Node and PowerShell touch hooks — a subdirectory edit no longer vanishes from the stop-hook scan.
- The temp-sweep cadence is now deterministic: a 24-hour marker-file gate replaces a randomized-probability throttle, in both Node and PowerShell; the PowerShell sweep also clears legacy marker files from a prior naming scheme.
- Legacy v3.0.0 config key names work again alongside the current names, in all five hooks; the README schema table no longer contradicts the canonical keys.
- Hook stdin is now BOM-hardened — some shells prepend a byte-order mark when piping JSON, which previously broke parsing.
- Config is now read once per hook invocation instead of 4-5 times with a git-root walk each time.
- Skill docs conform to one canonical structure (Fix mode before Output, one consistent heading name), and `/coalmine:stats` again advises `claude plugin update`.

Fixes a tier-rubric gap that could recommend a Heavy audit on ground already freshly audited this session.

### Fixed
- The tier rubric's freshness cap: when the scope was already audited at Standard or above this session, the recommendation is now capped at Light regardless of total score — previously size criteria alone could still recommend Heavy for freshly-audited ground, contradicting the rubric's own stated caveat. Caught live during the first dogfood run of the plugin-served skill.
